merger_name: Kanda Healthcare – Live Your Way, QLD

targets.name: LIVE YOUR WAY AUSTRALIA PTY LTD

party_page.name: Live Your Way Australia Pty Ltd

merger_description:
Kanda Healthcare Pty Ltd (**Kanda**) proposes to acquire 100% of the assets of the disability support business known as Live Your Way Australia (**LYWA**) through a business sale agreement (the **Acquisition**).

Kanda is an Australian care provider supplying a broad range of care services, including aged care, in-home care, disability support, community nursing, and children, youth, and family services in metro and regional communities across Australia. Kanda is a National Disability Insurance Scheme (**NDIS**)‑registered provider and delivers disability support services to NDIS participants, including in the Bundaberg and Fraser Coast regions of Queensland. Kanda does not currently provide NDIS-funded disability support services in the North Burnett region.

Kanda is controlled by Genesis Capital, an Australian-based private equity firm that invests in businesses operating in the healthcare sector.

LYWA is owned by Live Your Way Australia Pty Ltd and is a NDIS-registered provider delivering disability support services to NDIS participants. LYWA focuses on providing community access support services to NDIS participants in the Bundaberg, North Burnett and Fraser Coast regions of Queensland.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. the parties’ combined share of supply of NDIS-funded
disability support services in the Bundaberg and Fraser
Coast regions is low, and the increment arising from
the Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative providers of NDIS-funded disability
support services in the Bundaberg and Fraser Coast
regions, and in Queensland more broadly.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
